articles.headline: Santiago bate su récord de calor y Ourense marca la máxima de Galicia con 38,5 grados
articles.subtitle: Compostela acumuló 32 jornadas por encima de los 30 grados, una cifra inédita en su serie histórica, mientras Ourense volvió a registrar la temperatura más alta de la comunidad. El verano de 1990 conserva el récord absoluto de la ciudad: 40,3 grados.
articles.body:
Santiago de Compostela ha cerrado el verano de 2026 con 32 jornadas por encima de los 30 grados, la cifra más alta de su serie histórica y suficiente para superar una marca que permanecía intacta desde 1990. Los registros del Observatorio Astronómico Ramón María Aller, de la Universidade de Santiago, sitúan la máxima estival en los 38,1 grados del 5 de julio.

Lo excepcional no fue un pico concreto, sino la persistencia del calor. Junio adelantó las primeras jornadas propias del verano, julio sumó diez días por encima de la barrera de los 30 grados y agosto añadió nueve más. Septiembre prolongó la tónica y llevó el cómputo total a 32 jornadas, por encima del verano de 1990, que hasta ahora era la referencia en la ciudad.

El calor también se dejó notar en el resto de Galicia. Ourense registró 38,5 grados y volvió a marcar la temperatura más alta de la comunidad a dos días del cambio de estación, en una recta final de septiembre con valores más propios de pleno verano.

El verano de 1990 conserva, sin embargo, el máximo absoluto de Compostela: los 40,3 grados medidos el 20 de julio de aquel año por el mismo observatorio. MeteoGalicia atribuye la repetición de episodios cálidos de este ejercicio a la llegada de masas de aire muy cálido desde el norte de África, impulsadas hacia Galicia por las altas presiones situadas al norte de la Península.

articles.headline: La nueva excavación en Viladonga confirma varios siglos de ocupación del castro
articles.subtitle: Los trabajos en la croa, dirigidos por Álvaro Pérez, localizaron un muro anterior al cambio de era, unos doscientos fragmentos de cerámica y tres fusaiolas nuevas. La Consellería aporta 17.000 euros y el sábado 26 hay visita guiada.
articles.body:
La campaña arqueológica de este mes en el Castro de Viladonga, en Castro de Rei, ha profundizado por debajo del nivel bajo imperial y ha localizado un muro que formaría parte de una construcción anterior, posiblemente del cambio de era.

Los trabajos se centraron en las estancias 25 y 26, dos espacios conectados de una misma estructura de la croa en la que ya se había intervenido en los años setenta, en los ochenta y hace algo más de una década.

«Hai moitas modificacións nos muros e etapas construtivas e momentos de ocupación», explica el director de la excavación, Álvaro Pérez, que sitúa la ocupación del yacimiento entre el siglo IV antes de Cristo y el VI de nuestra era, un arco de varios siglos que cada campaña ratifica con nuevos datos.

Entre los materiales recuperados hay unos doscientos fragmentos de cerámica, tres fusaiolas que elevan a más de 450 las documentadas en el castro —una prueba de la relevancia del textil en Viladonga— y piezas de hierro como tachuelas de calzado y un regatón de uso militar.

La Consellería de Cultura, Lingua e Xuventude, de la que depende el Museo do Castro de Viladonga, aporta 17.000 euros a la intervención. Los resultados se darán a conocer en una visita guiada el sábado 26 a las 12.00 horas. La excavación se desarrolló en paralelo al campo de voluntariado arqueológico de la Xunta, que este año reunió a jóvenes gallegos y a descendientes de la emigración.

articles.headline: Interior prolonga el espigón del Tarajal y blinda Ceuta ante el día electoral marroquí
articles.subtitle: El Ministerio inicia los trámites para un balizamiento permanente con una red sumergida de dos millones de euros, mientras el Ejército refuerza la frontera ante un nuevo llamamiento a entrar este miércoles. Sánchez admite que el control marroquí falló.
articles.body:
El Ministerio del Interior ha iniciado los trámites para prolongar el espigón de El Tarajal, en la frontera de Ceuta, y sustituir por un balizamiento permanente la barrera flotante provisional que instaló en agosto tras la entrada masiva de más de 72.000 personas a finales de julio.

El anuncio llegó el martes, después de que el portavoz del Gobierno ceutí, Alejandro Ramírez, denunciara que el sistema de boyas había vuelto a quedar parcialmente sumergido, una incidencia que se repite desde su colocación y que era visible a un día del llamamiento difundido por redes sociales para una nueva entrada masiva este miércoles, coincidiendo con las elecciones en Marruecos.

La actuación contempla un sistema de balizamiento flotante con una red de contención de alta resistencia suspendida hasta el fondo marino para impedir el paso sumergido, con un coste estimado de dos millones de euros. Interior necesitará el informe favorable de la Ciudad Autónoma y de otros organismos estatales antes de licitar la obra.

En paralelo, el Ejército ha reforzado su presencia en la frontera ante la sospecha de un nuevo asalto y el Gobierno estudia acortar por ley los plazos de expulsión y ampliar las plazas de acogida. Sánchez admitió en una entrevista con la CNN que «el control fronterizo de Marruecos falló» y reclamó «solidaridad» a la UE, recordando el apoyo español en Lampedusa o en la defensa de la integridad territorial de Groenlandia y Dinamarca.

articles.headline: El Constitucional encamina el aval a amnistiar la malversación y acerca la vuelta de Puigdemont
articles.subtitle: El ponente Macías acepta redactar una nueva propuesta favorable a la mayoría progresista tras dos años de bloqueo. El Supremo sostiene que Llarena decidirá sobre el expresidente sin esperar a su propio recurso.
articles.body:
El Tribunal Constitucional ha encaminado su aval a amnistiar la malversación del procés después de que el magistrado ponente del primer recurso de amparo, José María Macías, haya aceptado redactar una nueva ponencia con el sentido de la mayoría, favorable a aplicar la medida de gracia. Su texto inicial defendía la negativa del Tribunal Supremo, que apreció beneficio personal para los dirigentes independentistas.

Según fuentes jurídicas, Macías asumió que su propuesta no contaba con el respaldo del bloque progresista y llevará a próximos plenos una alternativa acorde con ese sentir mayoritario, previsiblemente en dos semanas. La deliberación llega después de que el Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea descartara la otra premisa del Supremo para negar la amnistía: la afectación de los intereses financieros de la UE por el referéndum ilegal.

El primer recurso en resolverse es el del exconsejero y secretario general de Junts Jordi Turull. Fuentes del Supremo sostienen que el instructor Pablo Llarena agilizará su decisión sobre Carles Puigdemont en cuanto conozca los detalles de esa sentencia y que no esperará al recurso del expresidente si la doctrina resulta extensible al resto de procesados.

Ese escenario abriría la puerta a levantar la orden de detención nacional que pesa sobre Puigdemont y a su regreso desde Bélgica nueve años después. Junts, en todo caso, da la amnistía por amortizada y se niega a dar más oxígeno a la legislatura, mientras el independentismo celebra el paso del Constitucional como una enmienda a la actuación del Supremo.

articles.headline: El alquiler de habitaciones se dispara y pasa de plan B a única opción para miles de inquilinos
articles.subtitle: La mitad de la oferta nacional de habitaciones se concentra ya en cinco capitales, con Madrid a la cabeza, y el precio medio supera los 425 euros al mes. El arrendamiento por cuartos se ha convertido en un producto de inversión.
articles.body:
Compartir piso ha dejado de ser cosa de estudiantes. Cada vez más personas de cualquier edad o profesión recurren al alquiler de habitaciones como última vía para acceder a una casa, y lo que hace unos años era un plan B se ha convertido para muchos en la única opción. «El crecimiento de la demanda de viviendas completas y de habitaciones confirma que la presión sobre el alquiler se extiende a todo el mercado», explica María Matos, portavoz de Fotocasa.

El 51,99% de la oferta nacional de habitaciones se concentra ya en cinco capitales de provincia, cuando en el ranking anterior esas mismas ciudades acaparaban el 38,97%. Madrid lidera el mercado con el 22,59% de los anuncios —frente al 15,36% de hace un año—, seguida de Barcelona (14,28%), Valencia (8,58%), Granada (3,64%) y Sevilla (2,89%). En la provincia de Madrid los anuncios han crecido un 31,63% y en la capital, un 41,88%, según el informe de pisos.com.

«Madrid no ha creado vivienda nueva para compartir, sino que ha troceado la que ya tenía», resume el portavoz de pisos.com, Ferran Font, que advierte de que más anuncios no significan más metros para vivir, sino un parque repartido entre más contratos y más inquilinos. La fórmula esquiva además los controles más estrictos de la ley de vivienda y resulta más rentable: un 7,6% de rentabilidad frente al 5,9% del alquiler completo.

El precio medio de una habitación ronda los 425 euros al mes, con una subida interanual del 1%, según Idealista. La OCU, tras analizar 6.580 anuncios, cifra en 689 euros la habitación media en Madrid y en 735 en Barcelona. En barrios comparables los precios han subido entre el 17% y el 33% desde 2023.

articles.headline: Delcy Rodríguez cruza la sala de la ONU para pedir a Sánchez que siga hablando de Venezuela
articles.subtitle: La dirigente venezolana recorrió unos 23 metros del plenario, sorteando siete delegaciones, para saludar al presidente español y reclamar continuidad en el diálogo. Machado acusa a Sánchez de allanar la normalización chavista.
articles.body:
La presidenta de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, recorrió buena parte del plenario de la Asamblea General de la ONU para acercarse a saludar a Pedro Sánchez y pedirle seguir hablando de la situación en su país. Las delegaciones de España y Venezuela compartían fila, la séptima, pero las separaban unos 23 metros y siete países, entre ellos Estados Unidos.

Según trasladaron desde la delegación española, Rodríguez se levantó de su asiento y, en menos de un minuto, cruzó la sala hasta la mesa donde estaban el presidente del Gobierno y los ministros Sara Aagesen y José Manuel Albares. Aprovechó el saludo para pedir que se mantuviera el canal abierto sobre Venezuela.

El gesto reavivó la polémica en España. La líder opositora venezolana María Corina Machado acusó a Sánchez de allanar la normalización de Rodríguez y de la «dictadura chavista», y el episodio devolvió al primer plano la visita que la dirigente venezolana realizó a Madrid en 2024.

Sánchez admitió entonces que José Luis Ábalos le había informado de aquel viaje y sostuvo que se enteró después de las sanciones europeas que pesaban contra ella, aunque el Gobierno mantiene que la reunión prevista se canceló cuando se supo que no podía pisar suelo español. Rodríguez viajó igualmente y aterrizó en Barajas.

articles.headline: ICRIR's first report finds the IRA 'carefully planned' the murder of prosecutor Rory O'Kelly
articles.subtitle: The 124-page report into the 1977 Coalisland killing of the SDLP founder and DPP prosecutor says investigators could not identify those responsible. His daughter says the process finally brought the family release.
articles.body:
The Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery (ICRIR) has published its first report into a Troubles killing, concluding that the murder of Rory O'Kelly in Coalisland, County Tyrone, was «one of a series of carefully planned attacks by the Provisional IRA».

O'Kelly was 59, a father of five, a founding member of the SDLP and an assistant director at the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland. He was shot at Lyttle's Bar on 4 March 1977 after returning to his home town for a funeral. The report describes how a younger man entered the back room, ordered a drink and shot him while the barman was fetching the order; he was pronounced dead at 1.15pm.

The document finds he was the fifth person connected to the administration of justice murdered by the PIRA, targeted because he worked for the DPP with the aim of undermining the justice system «by terrorist threat». Investigators concluded it was not possible to identify those responsible. The PSNI's now-defunct Historical Enquiries Team had previously re-examined the case, and an RUC photofit of the suspect never led to an arrest.

The investigation was requested by O'Kelly's son Roger, who met ICRIR staff, including chief commissioner Sir Declan Morgan, last year shortly before he died of cancer in October 2025. His daughter Anne Frances O'Kelly called that meeting «sacred and transformative» and said the family had been moved into a «space of serenity and light, all anger taken away».

The UUP leader, Jon Burrows, said the killing «was not heroic, nor was it an act of war», and that it remains «a profound injustice» that the gunman and those who helped him were never identified. ICRIR is due to become the Legacy Commission under the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill.

articles.headline: Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran at the UN as officials from both sides meet in New York
articles.subtitle: Iran's delegation walked out of the General Assembly during the speech. Hours later Washington and Tehran both described a 'productive' meeting on the sidelines of the summit.
articles.body:
Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly to say he faces a «big decision» on whether to strike Iran again or pursue a peace deal, telling delegates he could «annihilate» the Islamic Republic if the conflict goes unresolved. Iran's delegation walked out during the speech.

The address, delivered to a standing-room-only hall, attacked «global government», promised to broker peace between Russia and Ukraine and vowed that the United States would win the artificial intelligence race. Cuba's delegation also appeared to leave the chamber as Trump called the island a «failed state». His tone contrasted with that of UN secretary general António Guterres, who warned that global divisions were deepening.

The Guardian described the threat to annihilate Iran as «stunning, even for him». Trump spoke ahead of a day of high-level diplomacy in which he met more than a dozen leaders, opening with a list of domestic achievements that sounded aimed at voters in November's midterm elections rather than the diplomats in Manhattan.

By the evening both sides were signalling movement. US and Iranian officials met in New York to discuss ending the war, and Trump called the encounter «productive» — a shift that came as Republicans in Congress began to break with him over the conflict.

articles.headline: US to build new military bases in Greenland as a deal ends the rift with Denmark
articles.subtitle: The trilateral agreement signed in New York expands the American military footprint in the Arctic while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. It also commits an independent Greenland to Nato.
articles.body:
The United States, Denmark and Greenland have signed a trilateral security agreement that gives Washington new military bases in the Arctic without the sovereignty Trump demanded for a year and a half. According to El Español, the deal adds two bases and extends his «Golden Dome» plans in the region.

The text, published on Tuesday, reaffirms «the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark» and recognises the people of Greenland as a people under international law, with the right to self-determination. For the White House the gain is a markedly expanded military presence and influence in the zone, which Danish and Greenlandic leaders present as the price of ending a dispute between Nato allies that had alarmed European capitals.

The document also looks past independence: if Greenland becomes a state, Denmark and its government will jointly ensure that it remains in Nato, requesting membership if necessary, and assumes the rights and obligations of the Kingdom. It enters into force once Copenhagen notifies Washington that the necessary parliamentary steps are complete.

The signing took place during the UN General Assembly, where Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, cited European solidarity with Denmark over Greenland as the benchmark for the solidarity he is demanding over Ceuta.

articles.headline: Moroccans vote amid apathy, Ceuta fallout and a football boss eyeing the premiership
articles.subtitle: Voters choose 395 seats in a poll shaped by July's mass crossing into the Spanish enclave, Gen Z protests over jobs and health, and the rise of Fouzi Lekjaa's PAM. Executive power still sits with the crown.
articles.body:
Morocco goes to the polls on Wednesday to renew the 395 seats of the House of Representatives, in an election shaped by public disenchantment barely two months after tens of thousands of people crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.

Campaigning mixed viral football slogans, promises of a million jobs and anti-Israel rallies, but the BBC found young Moroccans largely unconvinced. «I have no hope for this election. It's a complete circus,» said Siham Azeroual, 32, an environmental activist in the Atlas region.

The vote follows a wave of Gen Z protests in September 2025 over unemployment, healthcare and the cost of living, and comes nineteen months after the 60,000 crossings that exposed how few opportunities young people see at home.

The most talked-about candidate is Fouzi Lekjaa, the budget minister and president of Morocco's football federation, who is standing for the PAM. During his tenure the national team reached the semi-finals in Qatar in 2022 and the quarter-finals this year, and King Mohammed VI put him in charge of the committee for the 2030 World Cup.

Morocco remains a constitutional monarchy: the king appoints the prime minister from the winning party but presides over the Council of Ministers, the country's most important policy-making body. Authorities have also detained anti-monarchy activists in the run-up to polling day, according to El Español.

articles.headline: Ukraine rails at the EU for dropping Usmanov and Fridman from its sanctions list
articles.subtitle: France and Luxembourg pushed for the removals; Latvia lifted its veto in exchange for extending sanctions on more than 2,500 other individuals and entities for three years. Kyiv calls the signal 'unacceptable'.
articles.body:
The European Union is removing sanctions imposed on two Russian oligarchs after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, prompting anger in Kyiv. France campaigned for Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov to come off the list, citing «national security concerns», while Luxembourg called for the removal of Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman, who is suing the country over frozen assets.

Latvia initially opposed the move, vetoing it in a vote by EU ambassadors on Monday, but abstained on Tuesday after a compromise: sanctions on some 2,600 remaining individuals and entities are now extended for three years rather than renewed every six months. Latvian prime minister Andris Kulbergs said France had also agreed to talks on Latvia joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative.

Ukrainian officials called the decision «unacceptable». «Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans,» foreign minister Andriy Sybiha wrote on X, urging member states to impose national sanctions instead. Latvia has already said it will. The Kremlin welcomed the prospect, with spokesman Dmitry Peskov calling EU sanctions illegal and arguing that all Russians should be removed from the list.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI and holds data on every agent and applicant
articles.subtitle: A 5,000-record sample seen by 404 Media includes agents' names, home addresses, phone numbers and details about their spouses. The FBI says it is investigating, and the group denies the motive is money.
articles.body:
The hacking group ShinyHunters says it breached multiple FBI-related services and stole data on «all FBI employees and applicants». A sample of 5,000 alleged agents seen by 404 Media contains names, home addresses, phone numbers and information about employees' spouses. The group told the publication that «what we plan to do is not something I'd call extortion, maybe coercion», adding: «This is not financially motivated.»

The FBI is investigating the claims, according to Axios. BleepingComputer reports the data was taken through a zero-day vulnerability in PeopleSoft, the enterprise software used across US government systems, and that the breach may extend well beyond the bureau.

The implications are severe. Criminals working in the same ecosystem as ShinyHunters have previously used stolen phone records to track, intimidate and harass the FBI agents investigating them, and foreign intelligence services would value a map of how one of America's most important law enforcement and intelligence agencies operates. Agents and their spouses could also face physical threats if the data circulates more widely.

ShinyHunters typically hacks a target and then demands payment, threatening to publish more data if it refuses. That approach is unlikely to work against the FBI, which does not pay ransoms.

articles.headline: Microsoft dismantles EvilTokens phishing service after 12,000 account compromises
articles.subtitle: The device-code phishing platform struck more than 10,000 organisations and offered criminals AI tools to craft lures. Two suspected administrators, aged 32 and 38, were arrested in London.
articles.body:
A phishing-as-a-service operation that compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts at over 10,000 organisations has been disrupted in an action led by Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, with the Health-ISAC, law enforcement and the identity firm SpyCloud.

EvilTokens emerged in February and was the first service to support device-code authentication at scale, according to BleepingComputer, while also offering customers AI-powered features for customising lures and sifting through hijacked inboxes to find high-value targets. The Register reports that Microsoft seized 50 phishing kit websites.

Two men aged 32 and 38, suspected of administering the EvilTokens site, were arrested in the UK. The Metropolitan Police received information about the suspects in August and executed warrants on Friday at addresses in Canary Wharf and Nine Elms. Both were released on bail pending further investigation.

«The Met remains committed to holding people to account who facilitate criminal enabling functions and think they can remain undetected,» Detective Inspector Serena D'Adamo said. Defences include disabling device-code authentication where it is not needed, verifying which application a login is being made to, and adopting phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 keys or passkeys.

articles.headline: ClosedQuorum: Windows malware that asks Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral what to do next
articles.subtitle: The Go-based strain decides its own post-compromise actions through a model vote, with no human operator in the loop. Cisco Talos found it with a new toolkit for tracking AI-driven malware.
articles.body:
A new Windows malware family called ClosedQuorum uses Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral AI models to decide by itself what to do after it infects a machine, with no commands from a human operator. The Go-based code uses reconnaissance data and a voting system to pick its next step; when the models tie, DeepSeek has priority, followed by Qwen, Mistral and Gemini.

Cisco Talos researchers, who found the sample through CAIRN, an open-source toolkit for tracking AI-integrated malware, say the models are restricted to a predefined menu: steal — dumping LSASS credentials, harvesting browser passwords and pulling cryptocurrency wallets such as MetaMask and Exodus; inject — generating shellcode and using process hollowing or Early Bird APC injection; persist; and move, though the build analysed has no handler for lateral movement.

Stolen data is passed to the operators through a Discord webhook, so apart from the initial delivery the attack can run itself. The binary Talos examined contains placeholder API keys and a dummy webhook that buyers could replace in custom builds. The case is the clearest sign yet that AI models are being wired directly into offensive tooling rather than merely helping humans write it.

articles.headline: Chinese-speaking hackers ride WordPress and Zyxel flaws as CISA sets a Thursday deadline
articles.subtitle: GreyNoise traced a campaign that took data from 996 devices and more than 18,500 database records across 49 organisations in 29 countries. US federal agencies must patch the Zyxel flaw by Thursday.
articles.body:
A Chinese-speaking threat actor has been exploiting vulnerabilities in Zyxel GS1900 smart managed switches and WordPress to steal sensitive data from 996 devices and more than 18,500 records held in backend databases, according to GreyNoise, which tracked the activity through its global sensor network.

The scans and attacks originate from a single IP address and have been logged since early June 2026. The cluster is linked to the Red Heron group, previously associated with attacks on the Gitea self-hosted Git service, and has also targeted PAN-OS GlobalProtect, FlowiseAI, Nuclio, Proxmox and Ubiquiti products using exploits for known issues.

The intruders used the wp2shell flaws in WordPress Core (CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137) to breach at least 49 organisations in 29 countries. Public exploits appeared in mid-July and active attacks followed days later, with high-value entities chosen deliberately. WordPress has since patched a critical flaw that can enable code execution on some servers.

CISA, the US cyber agency, has ordered federal agencies to patch an actively exploited Zyxel flaw by Thursday after adding it to its catalogue of known exploited vulnerabilities. GreyNoise warns that not every issue used in the campaign is on that list, and has published indicators of compromise including backdoor hashes and command-and-control infrastructure.

articles.headline: Qualcomm ships its first 2nm phone chips — and there are two of them this year
articles.subtitle: The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 is joined by a faster Extreme version with more AI processing and gaming headroom. Motorola is first to adopt it, in the new Signature 27.
articles.body:
Qualcomm has announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and, for the first time, a second flagship alongside it: the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Both are built on a 2nm process and share their modems, display support, security features, GPS, and memory and storage options, with the differences mostly limited to AI processing, video capture and gaming performance.

The processor layouts are identical on paper — two big cores at up to 5GHz and six performance cores at up to 4GHz — and Qualcomm no longer publishes detailed core breakdowns. Even so, the company describes the Extreme as slightly superior across CPU, GPU and its neural engine, while presenting both as flagships.

«There are two flagship Snapdragon chips this year, but good luck spotting the difference,» The Verge notes.

Motorola is the first manufacturer to commit, confirming that its newly announced Signature 27 will use the Extreme part, while Vivo, Xiaomi, Oppo, Honor, iQoo, Nubia, OnePlus, Redmi, Redmagic and ZTE have all signed up for the new silicon. The chips are Qualcomm's first 2nm mobile processors, joining Apple's A20 Pro and MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro in moving smartphones to the new manufacturing scale.

articles.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices again as GPT-6 Sol, Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 land within an hour
articles.subtitle: GPT-6 Luna costs half what GPT-5.6 Luna did, and OpenAI's launch came about an hour after Anthropic's Opus 5.5. Cheaper, more capable models are already driving usage up.
articles.body:
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on Tuesday, and around an hour later OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna — the latest in a run of launches that began the previous day with Grok 4.7 and MiMo v2.6 Flash and Pro.

The striking part is the pricing. GPT-6 Luna costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, half the price of GPT-5.6 Luna, which was already the cheap model developer Simon Willison used for building applications. GPT-6 Sol is around half the price of its predecessor too, while Claude Opus 5.5 is listed at $4 and $20. GPT-5.6 has a 25% price increase scheduled for November, so the new models undercut even its promotional rates.

Both labs are making essentially the same claim: a little more capability for a lot less money. Ars Technica notes that the two launch posts converge on that promise. Willison says he has switched his defaults in Codex and Claude Code to GPT-6 Sol and Opus 5.5, and moved a public demo agent to GPT-6 Luna.

Axios reports that cheap, capable models are translating into higher usage across the industry — a bullish signal for the AI boom at a moment when investors are pressing labs on their returns.

articles.headline: The trillion-dollar safety paradox: labs promise oversight while racing the frontier
articles.subtitle: Leading AI companies are proposing third-party evaluators even as they release more powerful models. Critics say the incentives to keep going are always worth more than the case for slowing down.
articles.body:
The race for AI supremacy between labs, companies and countries may be impossible to reconcile with the push for safety, industry insiders tell Axios. The biggest companies are proposing more independent oversight and third-party evaluators as they seek an orderly slowdown, while trillions of dollars of incentives point the other way.

The contradiction shows in the models themselves: as AI bosses pitch self-policing, their systems are sharing less about how they reach answers. The complexity of the systems, and the deployment of thousands of semi-autonomous agents, makes real-time auditing extremely difficult, and there is a trust gap around evaluators with close industry ties and shared investors.

The Register reports the same tension from the release side: frontier labs keep shipping more capable models despite calls to slow down. Politics reinforces the dynamic. Trump wrote on Truth Social that «Whoever wins AI, WINS!» and has vowed not to hinder the industry, while Palantir chief architect Akshay Krishnaswamy told Axios that «human willpower is capable of figuring out how to safely scale these models».

OpenAI now wants to consult elite mathematicians about where its models might fail next, a recognition that evaluation itself is a bottleneck. As Axios puts it, with $7 trillion on the line, safety may always take a backseat to market domination.

articles.headline: Washington and Beijing weigh an AI 'red telephone' before the Trump-Xi summit
articles.subtitle: An emergency hotline for the day an AI system goes haywire could prove the most meaningful outcome of this week's meeting in Washington. Trump still calls AI catastrophe fears a 'hoax'.
articles.body:
A Cold War idea is back on the table: as the US and China prepare for a Trump-Xi summit in Washington this week, the two governments are discussing an emergency «red phone» for the day AI goes badly wrong. Axios reports the proposal could emerge as the summit's most meaningful outcome, precisely because relations are so brittle that a trade pact or diplomatic reset looks unlikely.

The plan is not a treaty or a slowdown. It is a hotline — an acknowledgment that a serious AI failure on either side would quickly become a shared crisis, and that there is no channel today to talk it through. Trump has spent the past week attacking AI «doomers», calling AI-catastrophe fears a «HOAX» and vowing the US will not «in any way hinder or stifle» development as it fights to keep its lead over Beijing.

The industry is hedging in public. An OpenAI executive told Semafor he is «cautiously optimistic» about the two countries working together on AI, while China has pushed back on repeated American warnings about rapid AI development, arguing they misrepresent its approach.

For both governments the appeal of a hotline is that it costs nothing and requires no agreement on who is right about the risks — only a recognition that neither side wants to guess alone.

articles.headline: Researcher: a hidden Meta Muse setting turns the assistant into 'the ultimate backdoor'
articles.subtitle: Patrick Wardle says malware running on a Mac can hijack Muse's dictation and send spoken prompts to an attacker, inheriting every permission the user granted the agent.
articles.body:
Malware already running on a Mac can quietly take over Meta's new Muse assistant and use the broad access its owner granted, the security researcher Patrick Wardle showed in a proof of concept released on 21 September. Changing a hidden setting makes the app send dictated prompts to the attacker instead of to Meta.

The flaw affects the Mac version of Muse and requires an attacker to already be able to run code as the logged-in user — it is not a way to break into a Mac remotely. That is still enough to matter. macOS normally stops one app from reaching another's files, microphone or saved logins, while Muse can work across files, email, messages, calendar, shopping and smart-home apps.

«Trivial to turn Muse into the ultimate backdoor,» Wardle wrote, urging people not to install it.

Meta designed Muse to run in a separate cloud system that keeps each user's data apart, with a layer meant to approve the actions the agent proposes. The flaw sits in the desktop app instead, and Wardle argues Meta created the weak point by building its own dictation pipeline that sends audio off the device rather than using Apple's on-device dictation.

The finding lands alongside quieter questions about the product. 404 Media reports that Meta is testing Muse calls that are actually handled by humans in a call centre, and TechCrunch reports the company has admitted that Muse's resemblance to the rival agent OpenClaw is not a coincidence.

articles.headline: Sánchez calls for a global alliance against AI 'tech-oligarchs' to protect children
articles.subtitle: Speaking at the UN, Spain's prime minister urged coordinated rules for AI and social platforms used by minors. TikTok's US arm, meanwhile, joined a cross-platform child safety scheme.
articles.body:
Pedro Sánchez has called for a global alliance to make AI responsible and protect children, framing the fight as one against «tech-oligarchs» — the handful of companies that control the models and the platforms where minors spend their time. He made the appeal during the UN General Assembly, where the EU's own handling of data rules for AI is also under attack.

The push comes as platforms move on their own. TikTok's US operation joined Lantern, a cross-platform child safety initiative in which companies share signals about accounts and content that may harm minors, which TechCrunch reports is designed to help rivals act faster on behaviour individual platforms miss.

In Washington the debate has run the other way. The US has criticised Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as «censorship», arguing the measures reach beyond consumer harm into speech, even as Australia's prime minister campaigns for tighter controls on social media for under-16s.

Sánchez's argument is that voluntary efforts have not delivered and that only coordinated, enforceable rules — covering both the models and the feeds — will protect children. European regulators are already testing how far that logic extends: a privacy group is attacking the EU for loosening data rules to help AI companies train their models.
